method: Close complete module contracts and end-to-end flows, implementing other-module dependencies as needed. File count is only commit minimum, never module completion. No standalone UI expansion while higher-priority module blockers have an implementable next step.
adjustmentRule: Module boundaries/admin wire protocol/native DTOs may change when actual interoperability/capability requires it. Record the concrete failed flow, change both producer and consumer and tests together. Breaking wire changes get explicit new protocol/version/evidence; do not silently redefine historical SHA-bound frames or add v1 data/protocol migration. Source-neutral identity, current authorization, owner consent/privacy, bounded actual ownership remain invariants.
progressRule: Each increment chooses a named closure gap with executable acceptance. A missing external prerequisite must name owner/exit condition and be kept fail-closed; continue independent implementable paths rather than indefinitely research/retry the same blocker. Commit only >=10 meaningful code files (current stricter runtime-source minimum), with module-scope result and remaining dependency gates stated.

modules.owns: Actual process routing, one native app startup owner, minimal locked shell/control inspection versus old-data business access, source-decision lifetime and resource handoff
modules.designExit: Every process/component path has explicit ownership, source context, allowed operations, fail/unknown route; no first-click/metadata/debug unlock
modules.implementationExit: Exact main process creates one startup owner; children/unknown do not. Old permits/resources never reactivate on observed source lock or different native source incarnation. Cross-module DB/catalog/runtime/task pins reject old-context reuse; old owned work still settles/stops without new access
